extraction_text: The ascetic Galava persistently insisted on something, and Vishvamitra became annoyed.
Vishvamitra told Galava to bring him eight hundred moon-white horses with one black ear and not to delay.

Galava lamented his poverty, failure, inability to repay his teacher, and the sin of being a liar and ungrateful person.
Galava decided to go to Vishnu-Krishna, the chief of gods and lord of the three worlds, seeking his help.
Garuda, son of Vinata, appeared before Galava, offering help as a friend.
